comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Additional live evidence of the drain's steady-state cost, plus a scope boundary.

During /rebar-debug of the plan-review sign fence (2026-08-22), `rebar doctor` caught a detached enrich_drain child (pid 96630, spawned by the impl-2ddd-b session) holding the advisory enrich-drain lock 437s at 0.0% CPU before exiting -- i.e. blocked in a no-timeout network call (the enrich LLM) INSIDE the advisory lock, not computing. A successor child (pid 41121) then held it 131s+. So under sustained load the drain is near-continuously lock-held, consistent with this ticket's budget-overrun symptom.

Scope note for the dedicated-clone remedy (approved on the related drain ticket): isolating the drain in its own tracker clone is the right fix for the drain's OWN latency / long lock-hold here, but it does NOT fix the plan-review sign-fence bug (a83f-6348-a08c-401d). I measured the sign-fence HEAD churn as 100% foreground ticket writes with 0 drain digest commits across 21 collect() windows -- so the two problems have different churn sources and need separate fixes. Keep them decoupled.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
POST-3d57 ASSESSMENT (2026-08-22, /rebar-debug Phase 1 discipline, worktree at 8481a057b69 = origin/main, includes 14aa285f963 / change 2123). Question: does 3d57's pin-health fix resolve the gate-check overruns? ANSWER: NO — the mechanism is independent and fully persists post-fix. Verdict: architectural (operator decision needed), per this ticket's own "Decision needed" framing.

MEASUREMENTS ON THE LIVE STORE (5,269 tickets, multi-session load, post-14aa285f963):
- `rebar claim` on this ticket: gate warning "took 2296.7 ms (> 20 ms budget)"; command wall 53.5s (most of the rest was tickets-branch push contention/retry).
- Instrumented `queue.pending_enrichment` probes: cold/full scan 8097.7 ms; marker-scoped probes 2840.8 / 2870.8 / 3249.7 ms. Same order as the pre-fix 339-3589 ms observations — no improvement.
- `rebar enrich status`: {"pending": 1046, "claimed": 0, "soaking": 1} — a ~1,050-entry standing backlog (~20% of the store).
- Drain lock free at probe time, one detached drain child running (pid 52083, spawned from a retired impl worktree's venv, 0:24 CPU).

WHY 3d57 DID NOT FIX IT: change 2123 touched only pin health (relation_snapshot child-index snapshot); zero commits to llm/enrich_drain.py or llm/overlap/queue.py between 14aa285f963 and HEAD. 3d57's own RCA rejected the enrich gate as the show-stall driver (rival (c)) and recorded it as a separate write-path mechanism — confirmed here empirically.

MECHANISM, REFINED (beyond the marker-clear story in the description): the task-4144 live-set fast path is ENGAGED and still costs ~3s, because the scoped walk is O(backlog) — it re-reduces all ~1,049 live entries per probe. So the overrun no longer needs marker churn at all: the standing backlog alone prices every probe at seconds. The backlog stands because drain throughput is structurally below the enqueue rate: batch cap 5/run (overlap_drain_batch), and each run holds the advisory lock through NO-TIMEOUT LLM enrich calls (observed 437s + 131s holds, earlier comment) — minutes per <=5 entries against enqueues from every attest/cert (plan_review/attest.py:218) plus the drain's own stale-digest self-heal re-enqueues (enrich_drain.py:293). maybe_drain probes on BOTH write seams (event_append.py, push.py), so a multi-event command pays the ~3s tax repeatedly.

RELATED DATUM: another session observed tracker writes stalling minutes-long attributable to the enrich drain and worked around it with REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN=off. Post-fix I did not reproduce a minutes-long stall from the gate alone (53.5s worst command, dominated by push retries), but per-write multi-second taxes compound across a command's appends and across 20 concurrent agents; the off-switch workaround remains effective and safe (drain is deferrable by design).

WHY NOT A SMALL MECHANICAL FIX (verdict rationale):
- Budget recalibration or warning throttling (AC option) silences the observability without removing the multi-second per-write tax or the backlog growth — it would mask, not fix.
- An append-tolerant marker (per-ticket dirty set) fixes only the marker-churn arm; the scoped walk stays O(backlog) and the backlog stays ~1,050.
- The real fix must change the drain's throughput/placement contract — some combination of: (1) an existence-only gate probe (maybe_drain needs bool, not the sorted list — early-exit on first pending hit is O(1) when backlogged and marker-fast when quiet); (2) LLM calls moved OUTSIDE the advisory lock + a batch cap sized to the enqueue rate, or the already-mooted dedicated-clone drain (see 9c72 relates_to); (3) backlog policy for the standing ~1,050 (age-out/tombstone or bulk-drain). (1) is the cheapest and nearly mechanical but still changes the gate contract this ticket says needs a recorded decision, and alone it does not drain the backlog or shorten lock holds — the write-stall datum stays live.

DISPOSITION: not implementing under this assessment (operator instruction: architectural changes escalate). Options above are the decision menu for AC1. Ticket returned to open for the operator.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: OPERATOR RULING (2026-08-22, recorded before implementation): approved scope is ONLY option 1 from the post-3d57 assessment comment — make the per-write enrich-drain gate check an EXISTENCE-ONLY O(1) probe ('is anything pending?') instead of walking the O(backlog) pending-enrichment queue (standing backlog ~1,046 entries prices every tracker write at ~2-8s; this very claim paid a 7375.8 ms gate check). Options 2 (LLM outside the lock / dedicated-clone drain) and 3 (age-out policy for the standing backlog) are NOT in scope — option 2 is under separate design. Do not restructure drain execution or change what gets drained. The gate's DECISION semantics must be preserved: it answers the same yes/no it answers today, just without enumerating the backlog. This ruling is the AC1 'recorded decision on the gate contract': existence-only probe, rationale = cheapest fix that removes the per-write O(backlog) tax while staying marker-fast when quiet; drain throughput/lock-hold and backlog policy remain open under the option-2 design ticket (see 9c72 relates_to).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DESIGN (option 2, for operator approval) — restructure the enrich drain so LLM calls run OUTSIDE the drain's advisory lock. Design-only investigation (2026-08-22, Copilot CLI session); no code changed, no Gerrit pushes. Experiments ran in a scratch worktree (design-6148-exp, retired) against throwaway stores.

== 1. MECHANICS AS VALIDATED (path:line, working tree @ origin/main) ==

Two different locks are in play; the 437s/131s holds were the DRAIN lock, not the store write lock:

- STORE WRITE LOCK: `_store/lock.py` (`write_lock`/`acquire`, dual-window fcntl+mkdir, `.ticket-write.lock[.d]` inside the tracker). Protects invariant I5 (single locked append+commit path — docs/concurrency.md §I5). Held per-event for stage+commit only (event_append.py:166, 284). The drain NEVER holds it across an LLM call: each queue write funnels through `queue._append` (queue.py:82) -> `_seam.append_event` -> the locked append, acquired and released per event. queue.py:23-28 documents this explicitly ("a claim CANNOT hold lock.acquire across its own append... The epic's design is therefore optimistic").
- DRAIN ADVISORY LOCK: `enrich-drain.lock` sidecar via `stamped_lock.stamped_file_lock` (enrich_drain.py:108-116; stamped_lock.py:12-13: "These are NOT store write locks: they only stop two PROCESSES doing redundant work"). The correctness boundary is the per-ticket optimistic CLAIM_ENRICH + lease (queue.py:454 `claim`, stamped_lock.py accepted-race comment) — the drain lock protects NO store invariant, only LLM spend.

The defect: `drain()` acquires the drain lock (enrich_drain.py:272) and holds it in a `finally` (:320) across the WHOLE batch — self-heal re-enqueues (:290-293), the pending scan (:295), and up to `overlap_drain_batch=5` (llm/config.py:150) SEQUENTIAL `enrich()` LLM calls (:309) plus 3 store appends+pushes per item (claim :300, digest emit :310, mark_done :311). Hence the observed 437s/131s holds. Meanwhile `maybe_drain` fires on BOTH write seams (event_append.py:357 via `_maybe_enrich_drain` :394-402, after the locked commit+push; push.py:591-598) and, while anything is soaked, spawns a detached child per write (enrich_drain.py:393-396) — every one of which hits the held lock and exits `{"skipped": "lock-held"}` (:275-281). So the system is structurally single-flight: throughput ceiling = 5 tickets per lock-hold (minutes), against enqueues from every certification (plan_review/attest.py:211-219, soak 60min, config.py:141) plus self-heal re-enqueues of every present-stale digest (:290-293) — and any post-enrichment ticket edit makes its digest present-stale (digest_sidecar.py:160-190, fail-closed), so ordinary activity feeds the backlog. The per-write ~3s tax is the gate probe `pending_enrichment` (enrich_drain.py:383 -> queue.py:414): with a standing past-soak backlog the marker cannot prove quiet, so every probe re-reduces all ~1,046 live entries (queue.py:426-440, O(backlog), 3 listdirs/entry).

Config doors (unchanged by this design): REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN off|async|always (config.py:149,437-439,723), REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN_BATCH (:150), gate budget (:151), overlap_soak_min=60/overlap_lease_ttl_min=15 (:141-142).

Dedicated-clone drain, validated for completeness: the store is the `tickets` orphan branch worktree (docs/concurrency.md §Storage shape). A drain in its OWN clone/worktree of that branch would append events under its own checkout's write lock (lock files are per-checkout), commit, and push to origin/tickets; convergence is the existing merge-as-union (I2 globally-unique event filenames make add-add merges conflict-free; §Outbound push). It is feasible and I6-compliant (leases, no new cross-client lock), but it fixes a DIFFERENT problem (foreground store-lock/push contention from the drain's per-item appends), costs a second store checkout + freshness lag (must fetch before reads), and does not by itself fix single-flight or the lock-across-LLM hold.

== 2. EXPERIMENT RESULTS (scratch stores, stubbed runner via drain()'s existing `runner=` seam) ==

E1 baseline (8 tickets, 5 enqueued soak-0, stub LLM sleeping 3s): drain lock held 19.8s for 5 items (15s LLM + ~4.8s queue-write overhead); 27/27 rival drain attempts during the hold returned lock-held (zero parallelism); foreground `rebar comment` writes were NOT blocked (median 0.20s = normal commit cost) — confirming the drain lock starves the DRAIN pipeline, not writers directly; writers pay via the gate probe and the drain's own append/push contention.

E1b gate-probe scaling: with live-but-SOAKING entries the marker fast path is O(1) (~0.1ms at 50/200/400 entries — `next_eligible` in the future proves quiet). With the entries PAST soak (the production shape) the scoped walk engages: ~10ms @50, ~150-195ms @200, ~160-390ms @400 pending, uncontended local SSD — linear in backlog, consistent with the measured 2.8-3.2s at ~1,046 under 20-agent contention. The backlog, not marker churn, prices the probe.

E2 prototype (`drain_v2`: claim-under-drain-lock -> LLM outside -> revalidate+writeback): lock hold fell 19.8s -> 1.5-2.9s (the claim window only, ~13x); two CONCURRENT drains processed 10 tickets with `llm_calls_total == 10` — claim arbitration gave exactly one LLM call per ticket, zero redundant spend, both drains productive.

E3 failure modes: (stale) claim, edit ticket, write back old-state digest -> freshness reads "present-stale" (fail-closed) and `_stale_digest_ids` re-enqueues — today's system tolerates stale write-backs already, at the cost of a re-enqueue loop; with revalidation the write-back is skipped and the entry re-enqueued pending (measured: stale_skipped=1, requeued_pending=true). (crash) claim with 1.2s lease, die before writeback -> entry claimed during lease, pending after expiry, next drain processes it (processed=1). (race) covered by E2.

== 3. OSS SURVEY — how others run expensive work against a lock-protected queue ==

- Sidekiq: atomic BRPOP reserve; job held in worker memory during processing, no Redis lock held (lib/sidekiq/fetch.rb:36-40); Sidekiq Pro super_fetch adds RPOPLPUSH to a per-process backup list + orphan sweep (wiki "Reliability").
- Celery `task_acks_late`: broker ACK deferred until after execution; crash -> broker redelivery / visibility-timeout expiry (docs.celeryq.dev configuration.html#task-acks-late).
- Postgres SKIP LOCKED queues — the canonical shape: claim rows in a SHORT transaction (`SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`), COMMIT (releasing the lock), execute with NO lock held, finalize in a second short transaction, with lease/heartbeat crash recovery. solid_queue (`ReadyExecution.claim` -> `claimed_executions` insert; process heartbeat + supervisor reaping), Oban (`fetch_jobs` CTE FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED -> state=executing; Lifeline plugin rescues stale executing jobs), pg-boss (fetch -> active + `expireInSeconds`; complete() finalizes), good_job (pg advisory lock per job).
- git itself: index.lock held only for the index mutation; fetch/push write objects to a quarantine dir with no index lock; `gc --auto` detaches and gc.pid only prevents CONCURRENT gc (git-scm.com/docs/git-gc, git-receive-pack §Quarantine) — exactly the pattern enrich_drain's module docstring already cites.
- Bazel Remote Worker API: lease PENDING->ACTIVE->COMPLETED with session expire_time; a missed heartbeat reassigns the lease (googleapis remoteworkers/v1test2/bots.proto).

BEST MAP: the SKIP LOCKED / pg-boss shape (reserve-short, process-unlocked, finalize-short, lease recovery). rebar's queue ALREADY IS this pattern at the per-ticket layer — CLAIM_ENRICH+lease is a visibility timeout, DONE_ENRICH is the ack, digest emit is idempotent (overwrite-by-content-hash). The only deviation from the pattern is the process-level drain lock held across the PROCESS phase. The fix is therefore a restructure of drain() alone, not new queue machinery.

== 4. RECOMMENDED DESIGN ==

Restructure `drain()` into three phases (behavior-preserving extraction along the existing seams, which also serves the complexity ratchet):

- PHASE A — COLLECT (under the drain advisory lock; seconds): self-heal re-enqueues; `pending_enrichment` scan; `claim()` up to the batch cap; snapshot each claimed ticket's state + `digest_sidecar.content_hash`. Release the lock. The drain lock keeps exactly its legitimate role: preventing N concurrent children from redundant SCANNING and stampede-claiming.
- PHASE B — ENRICH (NO lock held): run `enrich()` per claimed item. A hung provider call now blocks only this process's batch, not every other drainer.
- PHASE C — FINALIZE (no drain lock; store write lock per append as today, unchanged): re-read the ticket; if content_hash changed since collect -> skip emit, re-enqueue (staleness handled BEFORE the write instead of by the self-heal loop after it); else `ds.emit` + `mark_done`.

Lock discipline: store write lock — unchanged, never held across LLM (already true). Drain lock — shrinks from O(batch x LLM latency) to O(scan+claims) (measured 1.5-2.9s). Correctness boundary — unchanged: optimistic claim + lease; crash mid-B/C is healed by lease expiry (E3), a racing drain after lease expiry costs at worst one redundant idempotent digest.

Throughput: with the hold shrunk, the ALREADY-EXISTING per-write spawned children (enrich_drain.py:393-396) become productive concurrent drainers instead of lock-held skips — parallelism with no new spawner, scheduler, or CI trigger. Bound it with a cheap concurrency guard in Phase A (e.g., skip when `status()` shows >= N live claims, N configurable, default small — see OQ1).

Staleness: three independent layers — C's revalidation (new, prevents the wasted write), the fail-closed freshness reader (existing), the stale-digest self-heal (existing, becomes the backstop it was meant to be instead of a churn source).

Migration path: (1) land the drain() restructure + tests (single change, no event-schema or queue change, no store migration — the queue events and their semantics are untouched, so old and new drains interoperate: an old drain just still holds the lock long while new ones wait/skip); (2) separately decide the backlog disposition (OQ2) and the existence-only gate probe (OQ4); (3) optionally raise/adapt the batch cap once holds are short (OQ3).

Blast radius: `src/rebar/llm/enrich_drain.py` (drain() -> 3 helpers) and `tests/unit/test_enrich_drain.py`; possibly a small `queue.py` helper for the revalidation read; docs/llm-framework.md note. NOT touched: `_store/*` (lock.py, event_append.py, push.py seams), queue event types/reducer, MCP surface, config keys. Compatibility: REBAR_LLM_OVERLAP_DRAIN off|async|always semantics preserved; `overlap_drain_batch` keeps its meaning (claim-window size); trigger remains operation-linked on the write path — no CI-provider dependency, so project.portability holds.

Dedicated-clone drain: NOT recommended now. It addresses foreground store-lock/push contention from the drain's per-item appends, which this restructure does not — but that contention is 3 short appends per item, and the restructure removes the dominant costs (single-flight + lock-across-LLM). Keep it as a measured follow-on if drain appends still hurt after this lands.

== 5. OPEN QUESTIONS FOR THE OPERATOR ==

OQ1. Concurrent-drain cap: how many parallel drain processes may spend LLM $ at once (default proposal: 2-3, config-keyed)?
OQ2. Backlog disposition for the standing ~1,046: bulk-drain (≈1,046 trivial-class calls of $ spend), age-out/tombstone entries for closed tickets or entries older than X, or just let the restructured drain eat it?
OQ3. Batch cap: keep 5 (per-run claim window) or size to the measured enqueue rate once holds are short?
OQ4. Is the existence-only gate probe (early-exit bool for maybe_drain, kills the per-write O(backlog) tax) in this ticket's scope or a sibling ticket? It is the direct fix for THIS ticket's AC2; the drain restructure fixes the cause of the backlog that prices it.
OQ5. Stale-at-writeback re-enqueue: soak 0 (immediate retry, my prototype) or full soak (debounce a hot-edited ticket)?
OQ6. Should the drain's enrich() calls get a tighter explicit per-attempt timeout than the general cfg.timeout_s, given the observed 437s no-progress network wait?

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
FIX LANDED: Gerrit change 2140, merged as 59fad3133f9 (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1, no unresolved comments). maybe_drain's gate now calls queue.has_pending_enrichment — an existence-only probe that walks the same candidates (marker live set, else full store) with the same reduce_ticket pending predicate but early-exits at the FIRST pending hit; a quiet full walk still writes the gate marker.

BEFORE/AFTER, measured on the live store (5,269 tickets, 1,026 pending backlog, this host):
- steady state (marker-scoped, the per-write case): 2,792.8-7,557.5 ms -> 1.0-1.5 ms — inside the 20 ms budget (was 140-378x over).
- cold path (no marker, first probe after a queue append): 6,773.9 ms -> 117.5 ms.
- during this session, before the fix, live commands paid: claim 7,375.8 ms, comment 9,097.9 ms gate checks.

Warning rate: the steady-state probe meets the budget, so the per-command warning is gone. A cold probe (marker cleared by a queue append) may still exceed 20 ms once (~117 ms here); the drain's own pending_enrichment full walk rewrites the marker, so overruns are bounded to post-queue-append probes, not per-command — satisfying AC2's 'meets its budget or warns at a bounded, non-per-command rate'.

Regression pins landed with the fix (tests/unit/test_enrich_queue.py): scan-count test proving ONE reduction per backlogged probe at any backlog size (marker-scoped AND cold paths, counted not timed, mirroring test_pin_health_store_scan_count.py), a verdict-equivalence test pinning has_pending_enrichment == bool(pending_enrichment) across every reducer-distinguished queue state, and a quiet-repeat O(1) test.

Out of scope, still open under the option-2 design track (relates_to 9c72): drain throughput/lock-hold (LLM calls inside the advisory lock, batch cap 5) and the standing ~1,050-entry backlog policy.

compiled_state.description:
## Symptom

EVERY rebar invocation that writes (and reads that reach _store/push.py) under sustained multi-writer load logs 'WARNING rebar.llm.enrich_drain: enrich drain gate check took N ms (> 20 ms budget)' with N observed 339-3589ms on a 5247-ticket store — a permanent, warned-on-every-command steady state.

## Mechanism (proven during /rebar-debug of 3d57-602f-0b75-48ee — see its RCA comment)

maybe_drain runs on the store write path (src/rebar/_store/event_append.py:398, src/rebar/_store/push.py:594) and calls queue.pending_enrichment (src/rebar/llm/overlap/queue.py:414). The O(1) gate marker (task 4144-75d3) is cleared by EVERY queue append, so under sustained concurrent writes the fast path never engages and every command pays a full queue scan. The 20ms budget (llm/config.py, overlap_drain_gate_budget_ms) was calibrated for the marker fast path, not for the full-scan fallback at this store size; the warning itself is by-design observability ('budget is an observed target, not a cutoff', enrich_drain.py:379-385). POST-3d57 refinement (assessment comment): the task-4144 live-set fast path ENGAGES and still costs seconds, because the marker-scoped walk is O(backlog) — a standing ~1,050-entry backlog prices every probe at 2-8s regardless of marker churn.

## Decision (recorded 2026-08-22, operator ruling — supersedes 'Decision needed')

Option 1 of the assessment comment's decision menu: the per-write gate check becomes an EXISTENCE-ONLY O(1) probe (early-exit at the first pending hit), preserving the gate's yes/no decision semantics without enumerating the backlog. Rationale: cheapest fix that removes the per-write O(backlog) tax while staying marker-fast when quiet. Options 2 (LLM outside the lock / dedicated-clone drain) and 3 (backlog age-out policy) are explicitly OUT of this ticket's scope — option 2 is under separate design (relates_to 9c72).

## Acceptance criteria (re-scoped to the approved option-1 ruling)

- [x] A recorded decision on the gate contract, with rationale (the operator ruling above: existence-only probe; recorded as a ticket comment before implementation).
- [x] On the live 5,000+-ticket store under multi-session load with the standing ~1,050-entry backlog, the steady-state (marker-scoped) gate check meets its 20 ms budget (measured 1.0-1.5 ms, was 2,792-7,557 ms); overruns are bounded to post-queue-append cold probes (~40-120 ms, non-per-command), since the drain's own full walk rewrites the marker. Landed as Gerrit change 2140 / commit 59fad3133f9 with counted-not-timed scan-count and verdict-equivalence regression pins.
compiled_state.title: enrich-drain gate check runs 17-180x over its 20ms budget in steady state under sustained write load
